title: Scrambling Separates Superradiance from Quantum Chaos
authors: Long-Jie Li, Li-Li Gao, Zi-Cheng Liu, Zi-Min Li, Murray T. Batchelor
abstract: Early studies on the Dicke model linked superradiance to quantum chaos, whereas later anisotropic Dicke and Rabi studies reached apparently conflicting conclusions. We resolve this tension by distinguishing global chaos from local instability. Along the isotropic Dicke path, a sweep at fixed low excitation energy crosses both the superradiant boundary and a nearby chaotic window, explaining the reported correlation. However, the anisotropic Dicke model can be chaotic in the normal phase and regular in the superradiant phase, making superradiance neither necessary nor sufficient for global chaos. A fidelity out-of-time-order correlator (FOTOC), in contrast, probes the local stability of the stationary point selected by the initial wave packet. The superradiant transition destabilizes the origin, whereas a change in anisotropy can restore its stability and create displaced saddles. Wave packets centered at these saddles exhibit exponential FOTOC growth even on a classically regular Dicke energy shell with Poisson statistics. This local sensitivity also enables quantitative spectroscopy: combined with the topology of stationary points and local density of states relations, FOTOC dynamics reconstructs the absolute amplitudes of spectral singularities in both models without fitting the density of states.
summary: This paper clarifies the relationship between superradiance and quantum chaos in models like the Dicke model. By introducing the FOTOC, the authors demonstrate that local quantum instability (scrambling) can occur even when the system is classically regular, proving that superradiance is not intrinsically linked to global chaos. This separation is key for understanding quantum dynamics in interacting light-matter systems.
main_problem: The paper resolves the long-standing tension regarding the relationship between superradiance, global quantum chaos, and local instability in quantum systems.
main_result: Superradiance is shown to be neither necessary nor sufficient for global quantum chaos, as local instability (scrambling) can occur on classically regular energy shells.
method: The authors employ a combination of diagnostics: global chaos is measured via Lyapunov exponents, while local stability is probed using the Fidelity Out-of-Time-Order Correlator (FOTOC).
model_or_system: The study analyzes the Dicke model and its anisotropic variants (ADM) and the quantum Rabi model (ARM), using a shared Hamiltonian structure.
key_observables: FOTOC growth rates, chaotic fraction ($f_{ch}$), stationary point geometry, and reconstructed spectral singularity amplitudes.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($g_1, g_2$), excitation energy, and the distinction between isotropic and anisotropic regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between global chaos (energy shell properties) and local instability (stationary point dynamics).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the stationary-point geometry, showing that local FOTOC growth occurs even when the classical dynamics (Poincaré sections) are regular, separating local instability from global chaos.
paper_structure: The paper systematically contrasts global chaos diagnostics (Lyapunov exponents) with local stability diagnostics (FOTOC) across different parameter regimes of the Dicke model, culminating in a quantitative spectroscopic reconstruction.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical tool (FOTOC) to distinguish between different sources of quantum complexity—local instability versus global chaos—in systems relevant to quantum optics and cavity QED.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The new paper analyzes the Dicke model, which is a canonical model for collective emission, and its findings on superradiance directly relate to the physics of collective emitters, especially when considering local instability diagnostics like FOTOC.
